title: autotune: add default batching/caching profiles, quantization presets, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Subramanian
description: Motivation: reduce manual tuning and per-token cost for common workloads by shipping sensible defaults and tooling that surface unit economics. This PR implements: 1) default batching and KV-caching profiles derived from production trace analysis; 2) quantization presets (8-bit/4-bit profiles + compatibility checks) for common model families; 3) a small unit-economics CLI and API service that computes per-request token cost estimates given profile choices and hardware. Checklist: [x] add default_profiles.yaml and mapping logic; [x] runtime: integrate defaults into request routing; [x] quant: add presets + validation tests; [x] tooling: unit-econ CLI + lightweight UI hooks; [x] docs + migration notes. Context: ENG-1287 asked for autoset defaults after multiple incidents where manual config caused cost spikes; ENG-1299 requested faster engineer feedback on cost impact of config changes. This change is backward-compatible by default; customers can opt out. See internal playbook link: https://linear.app/ENG/1287 and docs prototype: https://docs.internal.redwood/autotune. Impact: estimated 7-15% unit cost reduction across sampled workloads in canary, with negligible latency regression. Rolling plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag, knob for strict/relaxed profile enforcement, and telemetry hooks to monitor quality regressions.
commit_summary: a12f3c9: add autotune defaults YAML and mapping code
b4d7e1a: integrate defaults into router; respect per-customer overrides
c8e9f22: add quantization presets and compatibility validation tests
d345f89: unit-econ CLI and lightweight API service for cost estimation
e7b1a6c: docs, migration notes, and telemetry hooks for rollout
review_thread: Initial review by Evan: requested clearer invariants around when defaults are applied vs customer overrides and asked for an integration test for a customer-scoped override. Author response: updated router logic and added tests (tests/autotune/defaults_integration_test.go) ensuring per-customer overrides take precedence. Sofia: asked for safety checks around quant presets causing numerical instability on older kernels; added compatibility validation and fallback to safe preset. Liam: requested unit-econ CLI to include sample hardware profiles and a mode to print expected cost delta; implemented. CI initially had a flaky e2e related to cached KV TTL; fixed by adjusting test timing and adding guard. After fixes reviewers approved. Final approval: Evan, Sofia, Liam.
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, quantization presets for common model families, and a unit-economics tooling suite to estimate per-request costs. Rollout is gated by a feature flag and is opt-out for existing customers. Recommended that platform and ops monitor autotune.autotune_cost_delta and autotune.quality_regressions metrics during rollout.
